target_customer: Developers and startups building web and mobile apps who need user authentication and related user infrastructure without writing it themselves
problem: Teams lose time building login, organizations, roles, payments hooks and user data plumbing, and closed vendors lock them in. Hexclave sells open-source, self-hostable modules for these jobs.
business_model: Open-source core with a managed cloud tier, usage-based pricing (tier details not verified)
product_category: Developer tools, authentication and user management infrastructure

founders.name: Konstantin Wohlwend
previous_startups: Listed on his YC bio as 2x YC, the earlier company is not named on the page
founders.background_notes: Education and employers taken from his YC company page bio; degree level not stated.

founders.name: Zai Shi
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the Stack Auth launch post referenced on the YC page; no background found in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Auth is well understood but security critical, and the product spans SDKs for several frameworks, a hosted dashboard and self-hosting, which is a lot for a team of two to seven.

defensibility.rationale: Open source invites forks and many open alternatives exist. Switching costs once user data lives in the system are the main lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is reported to have acquired or copied it. Neon later built a Stack Auth based offering and is now migrating users to Better Auth per Neon docs, which shows dependence on a partner channel.

market_need_then: Auth is a recurring pain for app builders, and the README positions the product as an open-source Clerk and Auth0 alternative, implying demand for pricing and lock-in relief. No dated spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Current domain hexclave.com; earlier brand used stack-auth.com per its docs host (docs.stack-auth.com).

identity.logo: Not described in any opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and technical, modular components pitch

rebrands.why: Reason not stated in any source found

branding.community_and_virality: Open-source GitHub repo and a Product Hunt launch listed as Stack Auth (YC S24); no sourced evidence of merch or fan content.

brand_strength.rationale: Stack Auth was a generic, hard to search name, and the later rename to Hexclave resets awareness. Evidence of brand pull is thin.

pivots.to: Hexclave, broader user infrastructure platform (payments, email, analytics, teams, vaults)
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the product pages only, date unknown

outcome_analysis: Hexclave is active with a small team of seven and no sourced exit or distress. It started as Stack Auth, an open-source authentication product launched around the Summer 2024 batch, and has widened into a user infrastructure platform under a new name. Funding is not verifiable from primary sources, so the trajectory is unclear.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists about 500K USD pre-seed (Sept 2024) with YC, Dealroom lists 125K USD seed, Seedtable lists a June 2024 seed with no amount.
